articles.summary: Eddie Murphy is attached to star in “The Chairman,” a drama series in development at Peacock created by Matthew Weiner. If greenlit, the project will mark his first-ever role in a live-action scripted series. Plot details for “The Chairman” are yet to be announced.
body: Weiner is best known for creating and serving as showrunner on “Mad Men,” which ran for seven seasons on AMC from 2007 to 2015 and is widely regarded as one of the best TV series of all time. articles.title: NAZA film-makers say they spoke to more than 100 sources about Israeli actions in Gaza
articles.summary: Team behind documentary push back against IDF attempt to discredit its exposure of military systems. The team behind the award-winning film NAZA, which details the Israeli military’s targeting policies in Gaza and its alleged acceptance of high numbers of civilian deaths, have revealed they spoke…
body: The disclosure came in response to an Israel Defense Forces statement seeking to discredit the documentary.

In its response, which the IDF said was based on statements made by the film-makers and a review made by a representative who had attended a viewing, the Israeli military claimed there were “substantial errors” in the film and that it had relied on interviews with two dozen intelligence and other troops who had only a partial picture of the target approval process.

At the centre of the IDF’s rebuttal was its often repeated claim that its rules of engagement explicitly distinguish between militants and civilians and prohibit deliberately targeting civilians, while requiring commanders to take steps to minimise civilian harm, claims that have long been challenged over the years by critics.
While acknowledging that it used AI to help recommend potential targets in Gaza, the IDF also said final decisions made on strikes, and the risk of civilian casualties, were signed off by officers.

articles.title: Halle Berry Accused of Child Abuse by Ex Olivier Martinez, Who Is Seeking a Restraining Order
articles.summary: Halle Berry is being accused of abusing her 12-year-old son by her ex-husband, actor Olivier Martinez, who has filed a petition for a temporary restraining order against the actress. Martinez alleges that on Sept.
body: In the request for a restraining order, Martinez contends that there have been “other instances of abuse over the course of the last few years. These other incidents involve additional physical attacks against our son, as well as verbal and emotional abuse from Petitioner to me.”

Martinez wrote in the filing that Berry had texted him to apologize after the incident. “I do not want to permanently sever the relationship between our son and Petitioner, but I do not believe that they should be interacting with each other until Petitioner can take sufficient accountability for her actions,” he wrote.
Martinez also asked that Berry be ordered to not be under the influence of alcohol or other substances while conducting visitation with their son.
“I believe he may be traumatized by the incident” and does not want to spend time at her house, Martinez said in the filing.

articles.title: ‘Fast & Furious’ TV Adaptation Ordered to Series by Peacock, Eyed for 2028 Premiere
articles.summary: The “Fast & Furious” TV series, first revealed to be in development earlier this year at the NBCUniversal upfronts, is closer to reality. Peacock announced Thursday that it has greenlit a new scripted television series based on the franchise.
body: According to Peacock, the streamer is looking to premiere the “Fast & Furious” series by 2028.
Premiere would coincide with the next film installment, “Fast Forever,” which has been slated to hit theaters on March 17, 2028.

“For the last decade, we have realized that the fans have wanted more,” Diesel said at the upfront in May. “They wanted us to expand the legacy characters, their stories. And for the last decade, the desire has been for us to enter the TV space that Fallon has mastered. And I had to wait till it was right… It became right when Donna Langley started to oversee it all, because that’s when I knew that the integrity of the characters, the international appeal, what makes us all feel like family would be protected in the TV space… The news that I have here today is that Peacock is launching four shows from the ‘Fast and Furious’ universe.”
Previously in TV, Netflix aired the animated series “Fast & Furious Spy Racers” for six seasons between 2019 and 2021.

articles.title: Oscars: International Feature — ‘La Bola Negra,’ ‘Fjord’ and ‘Woman Unknown’ Lead Early Contenders
articles.summary: Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis.
body: While we await the official tally, several contenders have already made their cases on the festival circuit. Spain’s “ La Bola Negra ” arrives with the TIFF People’s Choice Award, while Cannes has supplied two major players: Palme d’Or winner “Fjord,” representing Romania and the runner-up “Minotaur,” which will compete for France.

South Korea’s “ Possible Love ” also has significant momentum after Lee Chang-dong took the directing prize at Venice. And then there’s “Woman Unknown,” Denmark’s selection and the Golden Lion winner, which has perhaps the biggest question mark attached to its Oscar prospects as it still seeks U.S. distribution.

articles.summary: New York film festival: No spoilers here – TV’s grand illusionist meets his match when he moves in with Theranos founder and her family. For anyone remotely near the worlds of documentary, comedy or medical fraud, there has been one thing on the mind for weeks now: a single-minute clip of Nathan…
body: The prospect of TV’s grand illusionist versus emblematic girl-boss scammer seemed potentially too good to be true; buzz for You Can See Everything, Fielder’s furtive documentary co-directed with wunderkind du jour Lance Oppenheim (whose narrative feature debut, the Robert Pattinson-starring Primetime, premiered last month) was such that access to the film’s New York film festival premiere on Wednesday became this fall’s hottest ticket.

Let me say now, if you’ve made it this far: I will not spoil major shifts – and if you are at all familiar with the Fielder canon, you know they’re coming – for a singular movie whose enjoyment depends, in part, on an element of surprise, both for viewers and for film-makers who genuinely seem to not know what they signed up for when they walked into the Holmes-Evans household rental in 2023. Arguably the less you know about anything that is to come, the better.
Trust, ultimately, that you can see more than you ever imagined you’d see about Elizabeth Holmes and maybe get no closer to discerning the truth – and yet it will all be worth it.

articles.title: Tourette syndrome campaigner John Davidson to watch Bafta Scotland awards in separate ‘relaxed’ space
articles.summary: Decision follows independent review into handling of February ceremony, where his involuntary tics caused a BBC crisis. John Davidson, the Tourette syndrome campaigner whose outburst at the British Academy film awards in February led to a crisis for Bafta (British Academy of Film and Television…
body: In a letter sent to Bafta members on Thursday, the organisation’s chair Sara Putt and CEO Jane Millichip said that, after an independent review, Bafta had “strengthened and centralised our safeguarding, risk assessment and compliance processes” and had made arrangements in consultation with “safeguarding and inclusion experts” for Davidson’s attendance at the awards ceremony organised by Bafta’s Scottish branch, which is due to take place in November.

For the Bafta Scotland awards ceremony, Bafta says that, in accordance with Davidson’s own suggestion, he will “watch the ceremony via video link from a separate relaxed space within the venue with his family and friends”.

I Swear, the film based on Davidson’s life, is the leading contender with seven nominations at the Bafta Scotland awards, including all three nominations in the best film actor category, for Peter Mullan, Robert Aramayo and Scott Ellis Watson, and best film actress for Shirley Henderson. Aramayo unexpectedly won best actor at the national Bafta film awards in February.

articles.title: ‘These early friendships are huge romances’: Extra Geography’s lessons in teenage love
articles.summary: Rose Tremain, along with the cast and crew of a new film updating her 1950s story to the early 00s, remember the intensity of these relationships and explain why its story has not dated. A few years ago, Rose Tremain was asked to name her biggest disappointment. Her reply?
body: “I’ve been delighted by this whole project,” she says, still sounding surprised. Tremain adores the script, adapted from her elegant five-page story by playwright and Succession scriptwriter Miriam Battye. At their first meeting, Battye told her it would easily transfer to the modern day: “I felt really pleased about that,” says Tremain. “It’s not just a little relic from my past. It has relevance now.”

She is equally delighted with the finished film: “To make a 90-minute movie, Miriam had to do a lot of inventing. And I think all the inventing that she’s done is very, very right for the story. She completely understood it and yet made it her own, which, honestly …” Tremain pauses. “In cinema, I don’t know how often that happens. Usually when somebody says they’re going to write your thing, they take it in a direction which you can’t recognise at all.”

articles.title: Sexual assault case dismissed against Trailer Park Boys actor Mike Smith
articles.summary: Actor Mike Smith had been charged with sexual assault in 2025 for an alleged incident in 2017.
body: A judge in Nova Scotia, Canada, has dismissed the sexual assault case against Trailer Park Boys actor Mike Smith.
The trial was set to begin in provincial court in Dartmouth on Thursday, but after the Crown provided no evidence against Smith, the actor's attorneys requested the case be dismissed.
The 54-year-old actor, who plays the character Bubbles on the Canadian sitcom, was charged last year for an alleged sexual assault in 2017.

Prosecutor Bryson McDonald told reporters outside court that the Crown offered no evidence in relation to the charge "based on the Crown's ongoing assessment that the prosecution standard has no longer been met".

articles.title: ‘Kill Jackie’ Review: Catherine Zeta-Jones Leads AMC+’s Drab Misfire of a Thriller
articles.summary: A European art dealer goes on the run from seven ruthless assassins, whose assignment to take her out may or may not be connected to her checkered past as a high-flying drug dealer.
body: Several times in the first episode of AMC+’s Kill Jackie, the question comes up of whether its protagonist ( Catherine Zeta-Jones ) might be a bit bored.

One imagines it must have all sounded very zippy on paper, else it’s hard to imagine why creators Tom Butterworth and Conor Keane would have chosen to adapt Nick Harkaway’s novel The Price You Pay into a series. The elements of a juicy potboiler are certainly all present and accounted for.

Our antiheroine Jackie is not just an art dealer, but one who’s operated so consistently at such an elite level that not even eight-figure sales to billionaires quicken her pulse anymore — or maybe it’s just that this private-jet-setting life can’t match the rush of her old life as the dealer behind the world’s finest cocaine. But before she can decide what to do about this restlessness, the choice is made for her. An unseen someone has hired the Seven Demons, an elite band of assassins, to kill her, for reasons that are initially unclear but that Jackie reasonably assumes must be connected to her past. Jackie reacts by deciding to hunt down the killers before they can get to her.
